title: Sep 22 Results + Sep 23 Preview: Sixty Percent Is Good, But Let's Talk About Those Misses
summary: 9-6 on Sep 22 looks nice until you see how we fumbled the bag on some gimmes

content.value:
## Let Me Be Honest About Yesterday

Sixty percent. That's what we posted on September 22nd. Most people would call that a win. Most people would pop champagne and write some feel-good nonsense about "trusting the process." But I'm not most people, and this isn't that kind of blog.

Let's get real: we went 9-6, which sounds great until you look at the tape. We missed on a 61% Tigers pick. We whiffed on a 61% Cubs lock. And don't even get me started on that Rangers pick at 50% - what were we even doing there?

## The Ugly Truth Behind the Numbers

Yeah, we hit on the Pirates at 62%. Great. We nailed the Guardians and Red Sox picks. Fantastic. But when you're giving people 61% confidence and it goes sideways TWICE in one day? That's not variance, that's a problem.

The Rays split with the Yankees - we went 1-1 there, which is basically a coin flip dressed up as analysis. The Braves let us down at 51%, which honestly, anything under 55% is basically admitting we're guessing anyway.

## Tomorrow's Redemption Arc (Maybe)

Here's where I'm supposed to tell you that September 23rd is going to be different. That we've learned from our mistakes and the model is locked in.

But let's be provocative for a second: what if it's not? What if 60% is just who we are right now?

content.sub: 61% confidence · Framber Valdez vs Richard Lovelady

content.value:
## Why the Tigers Are Tomorrow's Play

Framber Valdez on the mound at home. Richard Lovelady on the other side. The model says Tigers at 61%.

Sound familiar? That's the EXACT confidence level we had on yesterday's Tigers pick that failed. So either we're about to look like geniuses who stuck to our guns, or we're doubling down on dysfunction.

But here's the hot take: Valdez is the real deal, and Lovelady's name sounds like a romance novelist, not someone who's going to shut down Detroit's lineup. The Tigers are at home, they've got momentum, and sometimes you just have to trust the uncomfortable truth that yesterday's loss doesn't mean today's analysis is wrong.

## The Bottom Line

60% wins. It's not sexy, it's not Instagram-worthy, but it's profitable if you manage your bankroll right. Tomorrow we're riding with Detroit at 61% confidence, and yeah, we know how that worked out yesterday with similar numbers.

But that's the game. You either believe in the process or you don't.

I'm 80% convinced we're right about this one. Which, ironically, is more confidence than the model has.
